title: The Bubble Nebula
caption: The Bubble Nebula, NGC 7635, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Bubble Nebula, NGC 7635 · constellation Cassiopeia · about 8000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #8 on ESA/Hubble’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble portrait shows the Bubble Nebula, also known as NGC 7635, an emission nebula about 8 000 light-years away in the constellation Cassiopeia. The telescope made this new image to celebrate its 26th year in space.

An emission nebula is a cloud of gas that shines with its own light. Energetic radiation from hot stars strips electrons from the gas atoms, and as those atoms settle back down they give off light at particular colors, which is why such clouds glow.

Hubble recorded this glow through separate filters for oxygen, hydrogen and nitrogen, each passing the light of just that element. Separating the light this way helps astronomers map where each kind of gas sits and how conditions vary across the cloud. Beyond this, the official caption gives few details about the nebula, and the image was released chiefly to mark the observatory's long working life.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (5.19 x 4.93 arcminutes) and distance (8000 light years), the frame spans roughly 12 × 11 light-years. Its light set out about 8,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This is a visible-light image from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, using filters that isolate the glow of oxygen, hydrogen and nitrogen. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The narrow filters pick out individual elements' light, so the colors are a scientific mapping rather than what an eye would see, and the gas is far too faint to view this way directly.
